thread:
incident-bot: ALERT 21:44 UTC — High KV cache growth + streaming token cadence stalls detected on serving tier (us-west-2). Automated threshold triggered: KV cache size > 92% for > 3m, streaming partial flush errors increased.

liz: seeing continuous_batching queues piling up on streaming routes, prefix hits stay, but KV page faults spike. latency p50 -> p99 divergence.

sam: can you paste the tracer link? I want to see where the partial flush is stuck.

liz: tracers: https://traces.internal/r/2179998888 - look at handler.stream_token_write -> partial_flush() loop.

jake: logs from node-gtw-17 show repeated `PartialFlushFailed` and `kv_eviction_pressure` messages:
```
PartialFlushFailed: timeout waiting for flush ack
KVCache: eviction_score=0.93 threshold=0.85 entries=4.2M
continuous_batch: queue_length=610 active_batches=24
```

maria: impact summary from support: 3 paying customers noticed truncated streaming sessions and elevated latencies. One reported client-side reconnects. Severity P1 for infra -> we should treat as high.

alex: rolling temp mitigation options: 1) rollback continuous_batching toggle to false for streaming routes, 2) raise eviction threshold to 0.80 -> 0.70? (but that risks more evictions), 3) throttle incoming streaming rate via ingress token bucket.

sam: prioritize fastest safe fix. Option 1 is lowest risk and reversible — flip continuous_batching off for streaming/* routes. We should also reduce batch_max_tokens to 256 to limit large-batch amplifications.

liz: agree. prepping control-plane change now. patch: 
```
PATCH /admin/routes/streaming/* HTTP/1.1
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "continuous_batching": false,
  "batch_max_tokens": 256,
  "kv_eviction_threshold": 0.78
}
```

ops-bot: DEPLOY STARTED by liz @ 21:51 UTC - change-id: cfg-2179998888-1

infra-bot: rolling change to 6 nodes in us-west-2 streaming pool, 30s stagger.

jake: applying CLI rollback on node group too: `rictl patch pool streaming-usw2 --set continuous_batching=false`

liz: applied. monitoring now. initial telemetry: continuous_batch queue drained from 610 -> 12 in ~90s, KV eviction_score down to 0.81 -> 0.74.

maria: support update ready: "We've applied a temporary mitigation to routing that should restore streaming stability. Engineers continue investigating root cause. We'll follow up with a writeup." Please add customer list.

support-bot: Affected customers: acme-platform, playlyft, clearview-api. Notified via support pings at 21:55 UTC.

sam: two parallel followups: 1) create a small canary patch that preserves continuous batching for non-streaming routes, 2) instrument more detailed partial-flush timing metrics and whether an ack path fails under heavy KV thrash.

liz: adding additional sampling hooks now. Also observed an edge case: partial flushes were queued but ack messages lost when eviction kicked in mid-flush. If eviction removes KV pages referenced by in-flight flush, flush loops retry and amplify batch queues. That's the perf cliff.

jake: reproducer notes: run a dense streaming workload with sustained long prefixes (>=1024 tokens) and interleaved high write-rate from rerank jobs -> triggers LRU churn and partial-flush failure. Putting in ticket.

ops-bot: New ticket created: INF-4893 "PartialFlush + Eviction race causing continuous_batch queue amplification" assigned to eng-runtime.

alex: next actions: short-term: leave continuous_batching off for streaming routes until hotfix ready; medium-term: patch runtime to make partial flush idempotent and ensure eviction marks in-flight pages as pinned until flush ack; long-term: add backpressure to rerank/write-heavy paths and smarter prefetch/pinning.

maria: customer impact estimate: peak error rate for streaming endpoints + truncated streams for ~18 minutes; overall requests affected ~2.1% of global serving for the window, but concentrated on us-west-2 streaming. Financially one enterprise support ticket escalated.

sam: ok. ops: please keep the change in place for 6 hours, then run controlled canary with continuous_batching enabled on 2 nodes with extra tracing.

liz: noted. setting reminder and will coordinate canary at 03:30 UTC.

jake: small hotfix prototype branch: `fix/partial-flush-pin` will pin pages during flush and short-circuit retries if ack already enqueued. Pushing tests.

infra-bot: metric alerts suppressed for this incident window per runbook to avoid chatter. Alerting resumed at 22:20 UTC.

support-bot: customer follow-ups scheduled: 22:05 UTC initial, 23:30 UTC update, postmortem email when available.

sam: thanks all. handoff: I'm oncall until 03:00 UTC; alex will take night escalation if anything re-escalates after 03:30 canary. If latency climbs back >50% of baseline or queue >100, page SRE.

alex: acknowledged, I'll monitor. please add notes to incident doc.

liz: adding remediation checklist to incident doc, including rollback cmd, canary plan, and action items for eng-runtime. Marking status: mitigated -> monitoring.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE 22:08 UTC — mitigation applied, queues drained, customer impact contained. Ticket INF-4893 opened.

sam: final: create postmortem stub and link to INF-4893. We'll schedule follow-up in the 48h retro. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
